question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{2}),$ calculate $P(1<X<4).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{2}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(1<X<4)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X<4) & ={\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x/2}{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =-{e}^{-2}+{e}^{-1/2} \\  & ≈0.4712\end{aligned}
$$
